article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Refined classic Haze hybrid
Breeder: White Label Seed Company
THC Content: 14–20%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: terpinolene, limonene , caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, pine, exotic wood, earth, incense
Flowering Time (Indoor): 50–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Mid to late October
Indoor Yield: 450–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 450–800 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

White Haze takes one of cannabis breeding’s most famous sativa traditions and reshapes it into a plant that is easier to manage without stripping away the qualities that made Haze desirable in the first place. Developed by White Label Seed Company, the cultivar was selected to retain the soaring cerebral character, running flower structure, and complex citrus-wood aroma of traditional Haze while shortening flowering time, reducing excessive height, and adding considerably more density and resin to the buds.

Those improvements helped the strain win first place in the Sativa category at the 2002 Cannabis Cup, an achievement still acknowledged by White Label’s parent company, Sensi Seeds . The finished marijuana has an unmistakably old-school personality: lemon peel, pine, dry wood, incense, and spice accompany an energetic high that eventually develops a warmer physical dimension. For growers who appreciate Haze but do not want to manage an exceptionally tall tropical sativa for four months of flowering, White Haze offers a much more practical interpretation.
Genetics and Lineage

The most accurate description of White Haze’s genetics comes from White Label itself: it is a new variation on the classic Haze strain, developed through selection and hybrid influence to increase resin production while reducing the height and very long flowering period associated with traditional Haze. The breeder also states that both sativa and indica characteristics are strongly expressed in the finished cultivar. What White Label does not clearly provide in its surviving description is a complete parent-by-parent pedigree for the original regular version. Numerous commercial catalogs list White Widow × Haze, but that formula should not be presented as definitively breeder-confirmed when White Label’s own material simply describes a refined Haze with substantial indica influence.

That distinction matters because the plant’s behavior supports the breeder’s description without requiring an assumed second parent. Traditional Haze genetics are associated with considerable stretch, loose running flowers, narrow foliage, long flowering periods, and powerful cerebral effects. White Haze preserves the elongated sativa-style colas but fills them with denser flower clusters and an unusually heavy coating of clear resin glands. White Label specifically describes those running colas as gaining density from the cultivar’s indica side. The breeding objective was therefore not to disguise Haze, but to concentrate its desirable character into a shorter, faster, more productive marijuana plant.
Effects and Experience

White Haze announces itself through the mind first. The early phase can feel bright, expansive, and noticeably euphoric, with a quick increase in mental energy and sensory interest. Conversation may become more animated, music more absorbing, and creative ideas easier to pursue. Unlike some highly tropical Haze cultivars, however, the experience is not defined entirely by racing stimulation. White Label describes a soaring cerebral high accompanied by a warm body stone, illustrating the unusual balance that helped distinguish the strain from more one-dimensional sativas.

Physical relaxation gradually becomes clearer after the initial cerebral lift. The body can feel looser while the mind remains engaged, creating a combination suitable for social situations, creative hobbies, walks, music, or an unstructured afternoon. Larger servings can push the experience away from clear focus and toward dreamy intoxication, particularly for consumers who are sensitive to THC. Because commercially available White Haze can vary significantly in potency, laboratory results from the actual flower should always be considered more reliable than a historical strain-wide THC estimate.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mental stimulation and moderate physical relaxation may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer a daytime or early-evening cultivar rather than heavily sedating weed. Some people gravitate toward sativa-dominant marijuana when seeking temporary relief from low mood, stress, reduced motivation, or fatigue, while the warmer body sensation may be useful to individuals who also want a degree of physical comfort. Appetite stimulation can occur as the effects develop, and the gradual relaxation may make the later portion of the experience more comfortable than the sharper high produced by some traditional Haze selections.

White Haze itself has not been established through clinical trials as a treatment for any specific disease. Strain names also do not guarantee identical chemistry, especially when cannabis has been reproduced by different growers over many years. THC-rich marijuana may increase anxiety, rapid heartbeat, dizziness, or mental overstimulation in susceptible individuals. Medical consumers should therefore judge a specific product by its cannabinoid and terpene testing rather than assuming that every flower sold as White Haze will deliver the same medical effect.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

White Haze carries the dry, complex aroma that made old Haze genetics famous. Sour lemon and pine appear prominently, followed by woody, earthy, and lightly spicy tones. White Label descriptions emphasize smooth wood and citrus elements, while surviving product information also points toward the familiar earthy-pine foundation found in Haze-derived cannabis. The profile is less sugary than contemporary fruit marijuana strains ; instead, it resembles lemon rind, resinous pine needles, dried herbs, sandalwood, and faint incense.

When the flower is broken apart, sharper citrus and spice tend to emerge from underneath the woody base. Combustion can emphasize earth and pepper, whereas lower-temperature vaporization may preserve more of the lemon and herbal character. Terpinolene and limonene are commonly associated with the bright herbal-citrus qualities of Haze-type cannabis, while caryophyllene could contribute spice and myrcene an earthy foundation. These are reasonable aromatic associations rather than a guaranteed chemical formula, since no single terpene profile represents every White Haze harvest.
Growing Information

White Haze was created largely to solve the practical problems associated with traditional Haze cultivation. Classic tropical sativas can stretch dramatically and remain in flower for many weeks, making them difficult to manage indoors. White Label selected this cultivar for reduced height and a significantly shorter flowering period while preserving its sativa-style flower development. Indoor flowering generally falls between about 50 and 70 days, with roughly 60 days being a useful target for many phenotypes. Secondary cultivation listings place indoor production around 450–600 grams per square meter under strong lighting and optimized conditions.

Stretch still needs to be anticipated. The plant develops elongated branches and running colas rather than the compact central structure of a pure indica, so topping, low-stress training, or a screen can help distribute growth across the canopy. Adequate support becomes useful as flowers gain weight late in bloom. Resin production is particularly impressive: clear trichomes can cover both flower surfaces and nearby leaves heavily enough to give mature buds the pale, frosted appearance implied by the “White” portion of the name. The same resin abundance also makes carefully handled trim useful for dry-sift or other concentrate production.

Outdoor cultivation works best where autumn remains reasonably warm and dry. Harvest typically arrives around mid to late October, depending on phenotype and latitude. Plants given unrestricted root space and strong sunlight can become substantially larger than indoor specimens, producing long lateral branches filled with multiple flower clusters. Yield figures vary too widely to treat any single number as guaranteed; commercial cultivation references range from roughly 250 grams to substantially more than 500 grams per plant under favorable conditions. Growers should prioritize airflow, branch support, and protection from prolonged autumn rain, particularly once the resinous colas begin gaining density.
FAQ
Is White Haze an indica or sativa?

White Haze is a sativa-dominant hybrid. Its cerebral high, elongated flower structure, and Haze character strongly express the sativa side, while indica influence contributes denser buds, a shorter flowering period, and a noticeable physical relaxation. White Label specifically describes both sides of the hybrid as strongly expressed.
What are the genetics of White Haze?

White Label describes the original cultivar as a new variation of classic Haze genetics that was refined to improve resin production while reducing height and flowering time. The breeder does not clearly disclose the complete parentage in its surviving description. Although White Widow × Haze is widely repeated commercially, it is better treated as a commonly published lineage rather than an unquestionably documented breeder pedigree.
What does White Haze taste like?

Lemon, pine, earthy wood, spice, and incense dominate the profile. It has a traditional Haze-style flavor rather than a modern candy or dessert character, with citrus brightness appearing over a dry, resinous, woody foundation.
How long does White Haze take to flower?
Indoor flowering generally takes approximately 50–70 days, with many plants completing bloom around 60 days. Outdoors, harvest typically occurs during October in the Northern Hemisphere.
Did White Haze win a Cannabis Cup?

Yes. White Haze Regular from White Label won first prize in the Sativa category at the 2002 Cannabis Cup. Sensi Seeds continues to reference that award in its current information about the White Haze family.
Final Thoughts on White Haze

White Haze succeeds because it does not attempt to modernize Haze by erasing its identity. Lemon, pine, wood, incense, long-running flowers, and an energetic cerebral high all remain recognizable, yet the plant finishes considerably faster and produces denser, more resinous buds than the notoriously difficult tropical sativas that inspired it. Its 2002 Cannabis Cup victory helped establish that balance as more than a cultivation convenience; the finished cannabis retained enough Haze character to stand out during one of the most influential periods of Dutch breeding.

Growers gain a comparatively manageable route into classic Haze genetics, while consumers receive weed that combines euphoria and mental stimulation with enough body relaxation to keep the experience grounded. Heavy trichome development, approximately two months of indoor flowering, citrus-pine aromatics, and strong production potential add practical value beyond the strain’s historical reputation. White Haze remains particularly relevant for enthusiasts who want old-school sativa character without committing to the extreme height and lengthy maturation associated with more traditional Haze plants.
